Look for trip edges over 1/2 inch, puddling after irrigation or storms, doors that stick or rub, and gaps under steps or slabs. Sunken panels next to intact ones, visible voids along slab edges, and cracked caulk lines also point to settlement. We’ll measure differential elevations, check drainage, and probe soils to confirm if lifting, void filling, or soil stabilization is the right fix for your St. George property. How long does the process take, and when can I use the surface? Most residential lifts finish in a few hours, and surfaces are typically ready for light use within 15-30 minutes after injection. Driveways and garage floors can often handle vehicles the same day. Commercial aisles and docks are scheduled to minimize downtime. We’ll confirm cure time on site, factoring in slab thickness, temperature, and the specific foam formulation used. Polyjacking vs. mudjacking - which is better? Polyjacking uses lightweight, closed‑cell foam (about 2-6 pcf) versus heavy mudjacking slurry (100-130 pcf), reducing the chance of re‑settlement in weak soils. Foam requires smaller holes (~5/8"), cures fast for same‑day use, and resists water. Mudjacking can be effective in some cases, but most St. George projects benefit from the precision, speed, and moisture resistance of polyurethane. How big are the drill holes, and will they be visible? Access holes are typically about 5/8 inch. We lay out a clean pattern, keep holes to the minimum needed, and patch them after lifting. On broom‑finished or exposed aggregate surfaces, patches blend well. On stamped or decorative concrete, we align holes with grout lines or patterns when possible to make them discreet. Is polyurethane foam safe and environmentally friendly? Once cured, closed‑cell lifting foam is inert and does not leach. privacy.text: > Privacy Policy Effective Date: May 9, 2025 This Privacy Policy describes how St. George Concrete Leveling (“we,” “us,” or “our”) collects, uses, and protects your information when you use our website or services. 1. Information We Collect We may collect personal and non-personal information, including but not limited to: Personal Information: Name, phone number, email address, address, and details about your tree care needs. Usage Data: IP address, browser type, pages visited, time spent on pages, and other analytics data. Cookies & Tracking Technologies: We use cookies, web beacons, and similar technologies to analyze website traffic and improve our services. 2. How We Use Your Information We use the collected information for the following purposes: To provide and manage our services. To communicate with you regarding inquiries, appointments, and service updates. To improve our website, services, and customer experience. To send promotional materials or special offers (only with your consent). To comply with legal obligations. 3. Information Sharing We do not sell, rent, or trade your personal information. However, we may share your information in the following cases: Service Fulfillment: When you submit an inquiry or request a service, we may share your contact details (such as name, phone number, email, and service request details) with a local business partner who will handle your request. Service Providers: Third-party vendors assisting with website hosting, email communication, analytics, and customer support. Legal Requirements: If required by law, court order, or government regulations. Business Transfers: In case of a merger, sale, or transfer of business assets. By using our website and submitting a request, you consent to us sharing your information with a relevant local business to fulfill your service needs. 4. Your Rights & Choices You have the following rights regarding your personal information: Access & Correction: You can request access to the personal data we hold about you and request corrections if needed. Deletion Request: You may request the deletion of your personal data unless we are required to retain it by law. Opt-Out: You can opt out of receiving marketing emails by clicking the “unsubscribe” link or contacting us. Do Not Track Signals: Our website does not currently respond to “Do Not Track” browser signals. For any of these requests, please use our secure contact form. 5. Cookies & Tracking Technologies We use cookies to improve user experience and analyze website performance. You can manage cookie settings in your browser. 6. Data Security We implement reasonable security measures to protect your personal information from unauthorized access, use, or disclosure. However, no method of transmission over the internet is 100% secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security. 7. Children’s Privacy Our services are not intended for children under 18, and we do not knowingly collect personal data from them. If we learn that a child’s information has been collected, we will take steps to delete it. 8. Changes to This Privacy Policy We may update this policy from time to time. Any changes will be posted on this page with the updated effective date. We encourage you to review this Privacy Policy periodically. 9. Contact Us If you have any questions or concerns about this Privacy Policy, please contact us . Governing Law This Privacy Policy is governed by the laws of Denmark. However, for users located in the United States, we comply with applicable U.S. laws regarding privacy and data protection, including the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA).
